summary:
Goiás recorded 5 killings of trans and travesti people in 2025, placing it in the national mid-band alongside Maranhão and Pará. Against a population of ~7.2 million the rate is about 0.69 per million per year, roughly 1.8× the national rate (80 killings across ~211 million). Goiás sits on the Cerrado agricultural frontier, and the ANTRA dossier finds 67.5% of Brazilian trans killings occur in interior cities outside the capitals - where monitoring, reporting and access to public policy are weaker - so a visitor away from the capital shares this interior exposure.

No Goiás-specific ordinance, legal restriction or protection measure was identified in the dossier; the state's risk profile rests on the above-national per-capita killing count and the interior-concentration pattern. The companion 2024 national dossier (122 killings, 16% below 2023) recorded the same ~68% outside-capitals share.

sources.summary: ANTRA's 9th annual dossier (released 26 Jan 2026, reported by SBT News): Brazil recorded 80 murders of trans and travesti people in 2025, 34% down on 2024 but with at least 75 attempted homicides and crimes marked by excessive violence; per-state 2025 counts - Ceara and Minas Gerais 8 each, Bahia and Pernambuco 7 each, Goias, Maranhao and Para 5 each, Alagoas 2, Mato Grosso 3; 1,261 murders over 2017-2025 (avg 140/year); 97% of victims travestis/trans women, over half aged 18-29, 70% Black among racially-identified cases; 67.5% of killings happened in interior cities rather than capitals, where monitoring, denunciation and access to public policies are harder; Brazil has led the global ranking since 2008. Lists Goias among the five-killings states for 2025.

ANTRA 2024 dossier coverage (27 Jan 2025): 122 trans and travesti people murdered in Brazil in 2024, 16% below 2023's 145 and just under the 2008-2024 average of 125; five victims were human-rights defenders, including a city-council alternate; 95.9% of victims were travestis/trans women; worst states: Sao Paulo 16, Minas Gerais 12, Ceara 11, with no records in Acre, Rio Grande do Norte or Roraima; at least 68% (83 cases) occurred in interior cities outside state capitals; 1,179 killings confirmed 2017-2024; official statistics are unreliable due to misclassification and underreporting. Provides the 2024 national baseline against which Goias' 2025 figures sit.
